headline: Five cups of coffee a day appears safe for adults

sources.title: Coffee lovers can take heart: Up to 5 cups a day appears safe for most adults, experts say
Coffee: Up to 5 cups a day safe for heart health, AHA says
Coffee and heart health: How many cups of caffeinated coffee are safe to drink each day?
Study: Five cups of coffee per day safe for most adults (video, NPR)

chunks.text: Most healthy adults can drink [[up to]] five cups of coffee a day without raising their risk of heart disease, [[according to]] a scientific statement from the American Heart Association published on July 20 in the journal Circulation. Five 8-ounce cups of black coffee {{add up to}} about 400 milligrams of [[caffeine]], the daily [[figure]] the review {{settled on}}. The number is [[the easy part]].

verbs.correct: To reach a total of a certain amount
verbs.wrong: To increase something by adding more
verbs.why: Add up to means that smaller amounts combine into one final total. Your daily spending, your weekly hours at work, or several small snacks can all add up to a surprising number.

verbs.correct: To decide on something after considering it
verbs.wrong: To become calm and relaxed after a while
verbs.why: Settle on means to finally choose one option after considering others, the way researchers settle on one clear number. It suggests a careful decision, not a rushed guess.

chunks.text: How the coffee is made [[matters]]. Coffee [[brewed]] without a paper [[filter]], including espresso, French press and Turkish-style coffee, contains cafestol, a natural [[compound]] that raises LDL [[cholesterol]], the kind linked to [[clogged]] [[arteries]]. A paper filter {{keeps out}} cafestol, and instant coffee does not contain it, so neither was [[tied to]] higher cholesterol. The caffeine is not [[the issue]]: decaffeinated espresso raised LDL too.

verbs.correct: To stop something from getting into a place
verbs.wrong: To stay within an agreed limit or rule
verbs.why: Keep out means to stop something from entering a place, like a filter keeping cafestol out of your cup. We also use it for keeping cold air, bugs, or noise outside.

chunks.text: Researchers reviewed 28 [[long-term]] studies and linked three and a half to five cups a day with a 20 to 30 percent lower risk of type 2 [[diabetes]]. Almost all of that evidence is [[observational]], meaning it [[tracks]] habits [[rather than]] testing them, so they cannot {{rule out}} that coffee drinkers [[differ]] [[in other ways]]. Caffeine was {{left out}} of the association's 2026 dietary guidance because the evidence was [[not solid enough]]. "What matters most isn't just how much coffee you drink, it is how it's prepared, what you are adding to it, and how your own body responds," said Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian.

verbs.correct: To say that something is definitely not possible
verbs.wrong: To give an official judgment on a question
verbs.why: Rule out means to decide that something is definitely not the explanation. Because the coffee studies only observed people, scientists cannot rule out that other habits caused the health difference.

verbs.correct: To not include something in a list or plan
verbs.wrong: To stop doing something for a short time
verbs.why: Leave out means to not include something in a plan or a decision, often on purpose. Something can be left out for lack of proof, for lack of space, or simply by mistake.

chunks.text: Energy drinks and caffeine shots are [[a separate case]], holding three to four times the caffeine by volume and linked to high [[blood pressure]] and irregular heartbeats. Sugar, syrup and cream can {{cancel out}} whatever benefit the coffee brings, and how fast a body {{breaks caffeine down}} [[varies]] with age, medication and genetics. Five cups is a [[ceiling]], not [[a target]].

verbs.correct: To remove the effect of something else
verbs.wrong: To stop an event before it happens
verbs.why: Cancel out means that one thing removes the effect of another, so they balance to nothing. Sugar and cream in your coffee can cancel out any health benefit from the coffee itself.

verbs.correct: To separate a substance into simpler parts
verbs.wrong: To stop working correctly for a while
verbs.why: Break down means to separate something into smaller, simpler parts, especially in chemistry or digestion. Your body slowly breaks down caffeine over several hours, and that speed depends on the person.

mainIdea.s: A major heart health group says adults can safely drink up to five cups of coffee a day. But how the coffee is brewed matters, since unfiltered coffee can raise harmful cholesterol.
mainIdea.why: The American Heart Association's July statement backs up to five cups a day. But it says unfiltered coffee like espresso raises LDL cholesterol, while filtered coffee does not.

mainIdea.s: The review found that drinking coffee actually lowers a person's risk of heart disease and diabetes. It also found that espresso is the safest way to brew coffee for a healthy heart.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the statement says coffee appears safe, not that it lowers heart disease risk. Espresso also raises cholesterol instead of being the safest brewing method.

mainIdea.s: A separate report found that energy drink sales rose sharply among teenagers in the United States this year. Officials warned that heavy use is linked to anxiety and poor sleep.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a heart health review of ordinary coffee, not about energy drink sales among teenagers.

tf.s: The association left energy drinks out of its 2026 dietary guidance.
